transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you for seeing me. Um... I guess I'm here because... well, I hope I'm explaining this right, but I just can't seem to shake this feeling that I've kind of ruined things for everyone. 

I mean, I know it's probably my own fault, and I don't want to sound dramatic, but I've fallen a bit behind at my IT job, and I've sort of lost control of my apartment situation. It's really embarrassing to admit, honestly. I just feel like I'm letting people down, and lately I've just been thinking that I deserve whatever bad thing happens next because of it. 

Is that... is that the kind of thing I should be telling you? I just want to make sure I'm answering your question the right way.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for at least the past two weeks?

Um, yes, I suppose I have. I mean, I hope I'm not making a bigger deal out of it than it really is, but... yeah. Most days I wake up with this... I guess you could call it a flat, heavy sadness. 

It's not like I'm crying all day or completely falling apart! I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around doing nothing. But it's just that the things that usually reset me—like putting on a record, or cooking, or tinkering with old electronics—they just... they don't really reach me anymore. I try to do them, but I just feel kind of blank. 

Does that make sense? I hope that's the kind of information you're looking for. I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Have you noticed a loss of pleasure or interest in activities that you usually enjoy, like putting on a record, cooking, or tinkering with electronics?

Well, I guess... I mean, I don't want to say I've completely lost interest. I still try to do them! I really do. I don't want you to think I've just given up on everything. 

It's just that... maybe I don't get as much out of them right now? Like, I'll put on a record, and I'll listen to it, but it just feels a little more like going through the motions than it used to. But I'm still doing it, you know? I'm trying to stay active. 

Is that... does that answer your question? I just don't want to sound like I'm not trying.
Have you been feeling that you're letting others down or that you deserve to be punished for things you've done—or haven't done?

Um, yeah, I guess I have been feeling that way a little bit. I know I mentioned it earlier, and I really don't want to sound like I'm throwing a pity party or anything... but, yeah. 

I just... I've let things slip so much. With my job, you know, falling behind on tickets, and then the apartment is just... well, it's a mess. I feel like I'm making things harder for my coworkers and for my landlord, and I just can't help but think that I've ruined things for everyone around me. And because it's all my fault, it just makes sense that I should face the consequences, you know? Like I deserve whatever bad thing happens next because I couldn't just keep it together.

I'm sorry, I know that sounds really dramatic. I hope it's okay that I'm sharing this with you... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of what's going on in my head. Is that helpful?
Have you been feeling worthless or guilty about things, even when it might not be entirely your fault?

Well, yeah, I suppose so. I mean, I know we just touched on this, and I really hope I'm not repeating myself too much or wasting your time. But... yes. 

It's just this constant, heavy feeling that I've let everyone down. Like, falling behind on those support tickets at work, and then letting the apartment get so out of hand... I know maybe I shouldn't take it all so personally, but I can't shake the feeling that I've just ruined things. For my team, for the landlord... for everyone, really. And because I let it all slip, it just feels like I deserve whatever bad thing happens next. 

I know I probably shouldn't think like that, and I'm really trying to be more positive! I don't want you to think I'm just wallowing in it. Does that... is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I hope that makes sense.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently—like eating much less or much more than usual?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I think my appetite has been pretty normal. I still make sure to eat, you know? I don't want to skip meals and let myself get unhealthy. 

I might not be cooking big, elaborate dinners right now, but I still grab a sandwich or something. I haven't noticed my clothes fitting any differently, either. So I think my weight is pretty stable. 

I hope that's okay? Like, I know sometimes people stop eating when they feel like this, but I'm really trying to keep up with the basics. Does that sound alright to you?
Have you noticed that you're feeling more tired or low on energy lately, even if you're not doing anything physically demanding?

Um, actually, no, I don't think so. I mean, sure, I get a little tired after staring at the computer screen all day for work, but I think that's pretty normal, right? I wouldn't say I'm completely drained or anything. 

I really try to push through it and stay as productive as I can. I definitely don't want to be someone who just stays in bed all day, so I make sure to get up and move around the apartment. So, yeah, my energy feels mostly fine. 

I hope that's a good thing? I'm really trying my best to keep myself going and not let everything fall apart completely. Is that the kind of answer you were looking for?
Have you noticed that you're moving more slowly than usual or, on the other hand, feeling restless or fidgety lately?

Well, um... I guess maybe a little bit on the slower side? I really don't want to sound like I'm not doing my job, because I promise I'm trying so hard to stay focused and be a good employee. But... at work, I've noticed my hands will just sort of hover over the keyboard sometimes. 

It's taking me longer to answer even really simple support tickets. It's almost like... like my brain and my body are running on a delayed connection right now. I feel awful about it, and I'm really trying to snap out of it so I don't let the team down. I just hope that doesn't make me sound lazy or anything? I'm doing my absolute best to push through it. Is that... is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you had any thoughts about death or dying, or wished you were dead, or had thoughts about hurting yourself?

Um, no, no, I definitely don't have any kind of plan to hurt myself or anything like that. I really don't want you to think I'm, you know, a danger to myself. I know that's a big deal, and I promise I'm not going to do anything. 

But... I mean, I guess if I'm being completely honest, sometimes... sometimes I just catch myself thinking that it would be easier if I just didn't wake up. Just so... I don't know, so nobody would have to deal with me anymore. I feel terrible even saying that out loud, because I know I should be more positive and I really am trying to be. 

It's just a passing thought, though, really. I would never actually do anything. I hope you know that? I just... I don't want to cause any trouble for anyone. Is it okay that I told you that?
Have you found yourself having trouble getting started on tasks or following through, even when you know you need to, like at work or around the apartment?

Um, well... I am definitely still working! I really want to make sure you know I haven't just stopped trying or anything like that. 

But I guess, if I'm being totally honest, I have had to ask for a little bit of help lately. Just some, um, minor accommodations and asking a coworker to give my tickets an extra review. I've been making a few small documentation mistakes that I normally wouldn't make, and I just really don't want to mess anything up for the rest of the support team. I'm just trying to be super careful so I don't let anyone down. 

And as for outside of work... I mean, I still take care of things around the apartment, but I guess I am leaving a little less than I used to. I've skipped a couple of my regular board-game nights with friends recently. It just... it feels a bit harder to keep up with my normal routines right now, even though I'm really pushing myself to stay active. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound like I'm slacking off? I promise I'm doing my absolute best to stay on top of everything and be responsible. Is that... is that the kind of information you needed?
Can you describe how you feel while doing the activities you used to enjoy—like tinkering with electronics or cooking—compared to how you felt before all of this started?

Um, well... I want to assure you that I am still trying to do those things. I really don't want to sound ungrateful for my hobbies or like I'm just sitting around doing nothing, because I promise I'm still trying to stay engaged. 

But... I guess, if I'm being totally honest, it feels a little different lately. Most days, I kind of wake up with this... this flat, heavy sadness. And usually, you know, my hobbies would fix that. Putting on a record, cooking a nice meal, or just tinkering with some old electronics—those used to be the things that would completely reset me after a long day. 

But recently... it's like they just don't reach me anymore? I'll be holding a soldering iron or chopping vegetables, and I just feel sort of empty or disconnected from it. I feel terrible even complaining about it, because I know I'm lucky to have things I enjoy, and I really am trying to keep at them, just hoping the spark comes back. 

Does... does that answer your question? I hope I'm explaining it right, I just don't want you to think I've given up on the things I love.
How long have you been feeling this way? Can you pinpoint when these feelings started or if they’ve been going on for a while?

Um, well... I guess it's been a little while now. I really hope I don't sound like I'm just letting things drag on, because I promise I've been trying to push through it on my own and fix it. But... if I really think about it, it's been about a year and two months? 

It kind of all started when... well, there was a pipe that burst at my old place, and I was forced to move into this much smaller apartment. It was just a really chaotic time, and all my normal routines just sort of... fell apart. I've been trying so hard to get everything back on track since then, I really have, but I just haven't quite been able to bounce back the way I know I should. 

I feel a little embarrassed that it's been going on for over a year and I'm only just now talking to someone about it. I hope it's okay that it took me this long to come in? I really am committed to working on it now, I just... I wanted to make sure I was giving it my best effort before bothering anyone. Does that timeline make sense for what you needed to know?
Can you tell me if there was ever a time when these feelings were noticeably worse, like a specific period where you felt much more down or struggled more than usual?

Um, well... I really don't want to make a big deal out of it, because I know everyone has their ups and downs, you know? And I promise I've been trying my best to stay steady the whole time. 

But... I guess if I look back over the last year, it's mostly just been this sort of constant, low-level thing. I haven't really noticed one specific time where it suddenly got, like, drastically worse or anything. It's just been a steady struggle to get my energy and focus back since the move. 

I hope that's okay? I know sometimes people have, like, really clear dips or crises, and I feel a little bad that my answer is kind of boring. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. Is it normal for it to just stay kind of... the same, without any major drops?
Before this current period, have you ever had a time when you felt down, lost interest in things, or struggled in a similar way for a period of at least two weeks?

Um... no, not that I can remember. I mean, I've had bad days here and there, like anyone else, but never anything that lasted for two weeks or... or got in the way of my life like this. 

I really try to be a positive person, you know? I've always been pretty good at just shaking things off and keeping busy. So this whole... this whole experience since the move is really new for me. I hope I'm not making it sound like I've just been miserable my whole life, because I really haven't. Before all this started, I was doing okay. 

Is... is that the right kind of answer? I just want to be sure I'm giving you what you need to figure this out.
